subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & next steps + prompt sets / potential regression
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Lisa Park <lisa.park@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: model fit recommendations + next steps

Hi Alex / Lisa,

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the walkthrough of ACME's support ticket summarization flow. Quick recap + next steps from our side: 

What we heard
- Input: short support transcripts (~120–300 tokens), mixed technical/non-technical language.
- Output: 3-line summary + top-3 suggested tags, strict hallucination tolerance.
- SLOs: p90 latency <= 200ms token generation, budget target ~$0.08 / 1k tokens.

Recommendations (quick)
- For latency-sensitive routes: redwood-7b-quant (lower cost, good latency) as primary for most tickets.
- For higher-fidelity summaries on complex tickets: redwood-13b-v3.1 (pinned) with prompt tuning; avoid rolling to v3.2 without evaluation.

Artifacts I'm attaching/links:
- prompt_set_acme_v1.txt (starter prompts + eval set) [attachment]
- Benchmark summary (high-level) — will send PDF after we run your sample through our harness.
- Benchmark link: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/acme-2026-v1

Immediate next steps
1) Can you share a 200–500 message sample of anonymized transcripts (we can accept CSV or JSON)?
2) I'll schedule a 30-min tech deep dive with Priyom (solutions eng) to go over runtime/latency tradeoffs — are mornings PST next week ok?
3) We'll run an initial evaluation and recommend pin vs variant routing; if you want, we can prepare a canary rollout plan.

I'll follow up with a tailored benchmark and recommended pin/rollback plan depending on results.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
[attachment: prompt_set_acme_v1.txt]

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Park <lisa.park@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit recommendations + next steps

Hey Marissa,

Thanks for the recap — that matches our priorities. We'll pull a sample (200 anonymized tickets) and send it over by EOD Friday.

A couple quick Qs:
- What kind of latency/cost should we expect for redwood-13b-v3.1 vs 7b-quant in production?
- Have you seen any recent quality regressions on v3.2? Our infra team is sensitive to any model-version regressions.

I can do mornings PST next week for the deep dive.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Senior PM, ACME Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Lisa Park <lisa.park@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit recommendations + next steps

Hi Alex — adding Priyom from our solutions team to scope the deep dive.

Quick answers:
- Latency/cost ballpark: redwood-7b-quant -> p95 end-to-end ~140–190ms, unit cost ~ $0.035/1k tokens. redwood-13b-v3.1 -> p95 ~260–320ms, unit cost ~ $0.12/1k tokens (depends on batching).
- Regressions: we identified a small quality regression in redwood-13b-v3.2 on a narrow set of summarization prompts (largely due to a training mix change). We did NOT roll v3.2 globally for latency-sensitive production customers — for most enterprise customers we recommend pinning to v3.1 until we finish the diff/eval.

Attached is a short benchmark summary (redwood_benchmark_acme_v2.pdf) with our initial evaluation plan and the prompt_set_acme_v1.txt I mentioned. Also linking our ACME benchmark dashboard: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/acme-2026-v1

Next steps from us:
- You send the anonymized sample (csv/json).
- We'll run the sample against redwood-7b-quant, redwood-13b-v3.1 and the v3.2 candidate and share a diff report.
- If you prefer safety, we'll propose pinning to redwood-13b-v3.1 for the canary and provide a rollback plan.

Priyom — can you propose 2x 30-min slots next week (mornings PST) and confirm if we can run the eval on ACME traffic patterns?

Thanks,
Marissa
[attachment: redwood_benchmark_acme_v2.pdf]

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Park <lisa.park@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit recommendations + next steps

Hi Marissa / Priyom,

We pulled a 250-ticket sample and ran a quick sanity pass against our current prod variant. We also ran a smoke comparison against v3.2 (pushed to our test endpoint last week) and are seeing a noticeable drop in precision for tag suggestion and more hallucination in summaries. I've attached a short file with 6 example pairs highlighting the regression (acme_regression_examples.txt).

Impact: small but real — several customer support agents flagged worse summaries after we flipped to the v3.2 test candidate. We're not in full prod with v3.2, but this is enough for us to want a rollback if v3.1 continues to outperform.

Can you confirm whether you can:
1) Open an urgent ticket to run a diff report between v3.1 and v3.2 on our full sample?
2) Support an immediate rollback/pinning of ACME traffic to v3.1 if the diff confirms regression?

Thanks — we can be available for a quick call today if helpful.
—Alex
[attachment: acme_regression_examples.txt]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & next steps + potential regression (ACME)

Alex — thanks for the examples and the clear description. Sorry you're seeing this; we'll prioritize.

Immediate plan (proposed)
1) Priyom / Eng will open a support ticket and run a full diff (v3.1 vs v3.2) on the 250-ticket sample today. We'll attach a structured diff + sample-level metrics (exact-match for tags, ROUGE/semantic measures for summaries).
2) If the diff confirms the regression, we'll pin ACME traffic to redwood-13b-v3.1 and roll back the v3.2 candidate for your tenant ASAP. We can do this as a tenant-level pin so it doesn't affect global rollout.
3) We'll prepare a rollback runbook and ETA for you within 4 business hours of the diff finishing.

Vivek — looping you in for the rollback/pinning ops and to confirm the runbook. Priyom — can you take ownership of the ticket and confirm timeline?

Alex — we'll also include the benchmark PDF and the prompt set used for the diff in the ticket. Once pinned, we can schedule a deeper quality review and discuss potential prompt or model tuning before considering a safe re-release of v3.2 for ACME.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
